Naphthalene (C₁₀H₈) is a polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon consisting of two fused benzene rings. Each carbon atom in naphthalene is part of the aromatic system and has a trigonal planar geometry.

In aromatic compounds like naphthalene, the carbon atoms form three sigma bonds (using three sp² hybrid orbitals) and one pi bond (using the unhybridized p orbital). This arrangement gives the characteristic planar structure of aromatic compounds.

The sp² hybridization means that each carbon atom uses three hybrid orbitals to form sigma bonds (two with adjacent carbon atoms and one with a hydrogen atom or another carbon atom), while the remaining unhybridized p orbital participates in the delocalized π-electron system that gives aromatics their stability.

Therefore, the carbon atoms in naphthalene have sp² hybridization.
